correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northern opening and Tacalaya-labelled upper valley
correspondence.finding: The original annex map places the chosen opening on the blue Ñocadua-labelled headwater west of Santa Cruz. It shows its southward continuation past Yaitipiñe, Varaca and Azangallane through the Laguna Tacalaya-labelled setting, then Charaque, Pampuyo, Chaullani/Lacuyo and Pujocucho. The selected upper part follows this mapped drainage rather than merely lying inside the Locumba basin. The regional sheet does not delineate a broad Tacalaya lake crossing at this chosen passage; only the actual mapped through-corridor is asserted.
correspondence.named_reach_scope: Ñocadua-labelled opening; Tacalaya upper-valley setting, without exact name-transition assignment

correspondence.component_scope: Huayllani and Cularjahuira vicinity to the Camilaca valley
correspondence.finding: The map continues the selected course southward from the Pujocucho/Huayllani area, east of the separately drawn Cularjahuira dam symbol, through the southward then southwestward bend toward Calacala, Charipujo and Camilaca. The blue receiving course and tributary joins remain visible despite large provincial lettering. The nearby impoundment is not assigned as a through-reservoir passage of this selection. The report independently identifies the river at Camilaca and Cairani as Río Camilaca.
correspondence.named_reach_scope: Upper Camilaca corridor; nearby Cularjahuira impoundment is on a separate western branch

correspondence.component_scope: Camilaca through Cambaya and the Ilabaya upper valley
correspondence.finding: The selected southwestward valley follows the original mapped channel below Camilaca, past the Conmani/Cocajone–Cambaya setting and Toco Chico, then through Chululuni and the Calumbraya–Tarapampa/Minaitita area. The western drainage and the eastern Huanuara-side tributaries connect to the selected receiving valley as drawn. Field-report prose identifies the Cambaya-road corridor as Río Ilabaya. Different reach names do not interrupt the demonstrated geographic connection.
correspondence.named_reach_scope: Río Camilaca and downstream Río Ilabaya reaches

correspondence.component_scope: Ilabaya to the eastern Curibaya join and Mirave
correspondence.finding: The blue main channel continues past Colpachi, Ilabaya and Cocal to the Mirave/Ticapampa area. The map visibly joins the eastern Curibaya–Poquera corridor to this selected receiving channel and continues southwest beyond the confluence. The source report names Ilabaya locally; PET distinguishes Ilabaya and Curibaya as medium-basin rivers of Locumba. Aricota lake and its hydroelectric-return corridor lie on the eastern tributary rather than on the selected northern opening, so this finding does not invent an Aricota through-lake crossing.
correspondence.named_reach_scope: Río Ilabaya into the representative Río Locumba system

correspondence.component_scope: Mirave and Cuari/Coari to the middle Locumba valley
correspondence.finding: The map follows the selected southwestward course below Mirave through Cuari/Coari, Oconchay, Margarata, Los Troncos, Chipe and Sogollo. The Blancas and other side-drainage mouths meet this same valley, and the route remains separate from the nearby western Cinto branch and eastern La Cruz/Paenca drainage until their actual mapped joins. Every selected part boundary in this interval falls on the depicted receiving corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Cinto confluence and the lower-valley turn
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor passes the Mal Paso/Grande setting, receives the mapped northern Cinto branch, and continues toward Piñapo and the Chaucalaña-side valley. This is an observed channel junction, not a transfer of the name Cinto to the selected upstream mainstem. The report describes both Cinto and Locumba in the Locumba district, while PET identifies the connected medium basin continuing toward Camiara.
correspondence.named_reach_scope: Río Locumba with Cinto tributary join

correspondence.component_scope: Montero–Sitana–Camiara lower valley and diversion setting
correspondence.finding: The original blue channel tracks the selected southwestward turn past Montero, Sitana/Sitana Valle, La Aurora and the Puente Camiara/Camiarita area. It continues beyond the transport crossing and the mapped Bocatoma/Quebrada Honda vicinity. PET records the Canal de Ite diversion setting in the lower Locumba basin; the selected route stays on the mapped valley toward Ite. Neither the diversion nor adjacent managed works are treated as evidence that the selected downstream connector disappears.

correspondence.component_scope: Chical to Ite–Miramar coastal approach
correspondence.finding: The map continues the selected southward channel through the Chical area and the valley east of Tacahuay/Tanapache/Yarando, then past Ite and Miramar. The selected passage is distinguished from the separate western coastal quebradas and from the eastern Honda drainage. All four selected parts follow the visible blue receiving channel to the last coastal approach.

correspondence.component_scope: Pampa Baja–Puesto de Aduana actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The blue channel continues south past Miramar and Pampa Baja to the coast near Puesto de Aduana, south of Puerto Ingles. This matches the selected final part and actual terminal at ordinary river-mouth scale. PET explicitly places the Locumba outlet in the wetlands of Bahía de Ite. The map and prose jointly establish the wetland/coastal receiving setting; they do not establish exact present-day shoreline, wetland microchannels or perennial discharge.
correspondence.named_reach_scope: Río Locumba outlet in the Bahía de Ite setting

correspondence.component_scope: Selected unnamed headward lakes and short connecting channels
correspondence.finding: The opening lies in the western lobe of a small mapped lake north-west of Meelpaeg Reservoir. The lake-and-channel chain runs east, bends through a smaller pond and continues southeast toward the reservoir. The matching sequence and its joins are visible in the overlapping management maps. These small waterbodies and feeder reaches are not assigned the Grey River hydronym individually.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestern entry and southward Meelpaeg reservoir passage
correspondence.finding: The short southeastern approach enters a northwestern arm of the mapped Meelpaeg Lake reservoir. The selected route then turns south through the connected reservoir footprint. The management-map label establishes the waterbody name, while the operator account independently associates Meelpaeg Lake with the Grey River development.

correspondence.component_scope: Western reservoir arm and Pudops outlet setting
correspondence.finding: The selected reservoir passage turns southwest and west into the outlet arm. Read and Cole identify the Grey River diversion dam at the outlet of Pudops Lake and depict the river continuation below it; the modern management map shows the corresponding western exit and adjoining river. The separate eastward Ebbegunbaeg diversion toward Salmon River is not the selected continuation.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Grey River valley below the reservoir
correspondence.finding: From the reservoir outlet the mapped channel runs southwest, then south, through a narrow valley with small widened water sections and side-stream joins. The two management maps overlap across this interval. The provincial monitoring profile identifies the lower Grey basin as the altered drainage below Meelpaeg dam.

correspondence.component_scope: Central Grey River channel and widened reaches
correspondence.finding: The selected southward corridor follows the mapped continuous main channel through its elongated wider sections and intervening constrictions. Adjacent ponds and tributaries remain distinct from the selected mainstem; all selected joins are accounted for at ordinary corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Grey River bends and inland head of the marine inlet
correspondence.finding: The river turns southeast, then south and southwest, approaching the head of the long northeastern coastal arm. The management map places the Grey River label on this lower corridor. The station profile independently identifies a point along the same lower valley upstream of the settlement and marine outlet.

correspondence.component_scope: Grey River marine inlet and its actual selected seaward entrance
correspondence.finding: The selected line continues past the inland river mouth through the long northeastern arm of the coastal inlet, passes its junction with the separate southeastern arm, and follows the narrow entrance to the sea beside Grey River Point. CHS describes Grey River as an inlet with two arms and a narrow entrance channel. The actual selected tip is at that seaward entrance; it is not moved back to the inland freshwater mouth or into the separate southeastern arm.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen western Covão opening and Esperança-side continuation
correspondence.finding: The Esperança original depicts the selected western stream in the Riacho Covão and Açude Covão setting, followed northeast past Lagoa de Pedra toward Umburana. Its channel and small impoundment connections distinguish this opening from the separate southern Manguape/Mamanguape headwaters. The initial stored point is not treated as a surveyed spring or an official source definition.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward Covão corridor, small impoundments and northeast outlet
correspondence.finding: Overlapping Esperança and Remígio originals show the northward continuation west of Remígio, intermediate waterbody/channel connections, and the northeastward turn toward the Araçagi valley. The older map renders small impoundment water areas more explicitly than the newer generalized municipal map. No new reservoir name or present operating condition is assigned to these passages.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern receiving valley across the Areia, Pilões and Guarabira-side country
correspondence.finding: The Remígio eastern continuation and AESA river-hierarchy map show the selected northeast-to-east valley and its successive tributary joins along the northern Araçagi approach. They keep the southern Mamanguape headwater route, Saulo Maia/Tauá side approaches and the more northerly Bananeiras drainage separate. The regional line shapes and junction sequence account for these stored parts without assigning one label to every feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: Araçagi-side river, Mamanguape confluence and Araçagi impoundment
correspondence.finding: The Araçagi municipal original shows the western incoming river, its route through and beyond Araçagi, the southern Mamanguape approach, their connection within the elongated impoundment setting, and the eastward outlet. AESA identifies the corresponding impoundment as Araçagi. The municipal sheet prints Rio Guarabira on its western incoming reach and Rio Araçagi nearer the town; this label distribution is retained without resolving a precise naming boundary.

correspondence.component_scope: Connected lower Mamanguape receiving course
correspondence.finding: The reservoir outlet and lower named Mamanguape course continue east through the Cuité de Mamanguape/Mamanguape-side corridor, then northeast toward Rio Tinto. Source cartography distinguishes the river from the separately mapped Canal Acauã–Araçagi and from the Miriri basin to the south; the selection is not assigned to that engineered canal.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower river and estuarine wetland passage
correspondence.finding: The Rio Tinto original and AESA mangrove/river maps show the lower Mamanguape corridor continuing through the wetland and estuarine setting, with its tributary joins and larger downstream bends. The stored coarse line generalizes these bends; no exact bank or minor-channel match is claimed. Neither wetland symbols alone nor protected-area membership is used as the connection evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual final selected estuary-side segment
correspondence.finding: The final segment reaches the lower Mamanguape estuarine setting near Barra do Mamanguape. It shortens the mapped northward bend and lies toward the southern estuary-side margin, upstream of the outer Atlantic opening. The actual stored endpoint is retained: no surveyed mouth, exact in-water tip, or offshore continuation is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen eastern opening and northwest bend
correspondence.finding: Montilla locates the Carache basin and its high eastern terrain, but Figure1 only shades a basin on a political map. Neither that figure nor the two regional hydrographic maps resolves this chosen opening. No local feeder name is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwest return and northward upper connector
correspondence.finding: The full hooked approach and its joins remain unestablished. Carache and Monaicito occur in the state chapter, but those regional relationships do not prove this selected through-route. The chapter’s separate state-map appendix was not available within the acquired chapter.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward plain corridor approaching Agua Viva
correspondence.finding: Lámina111 depicts an eastern inflow running west to the reservoir, labeled Río Monay. González Cruz and Montilla instead discuss the Carache drainage and Monay plain. The ordinary corridor agrees, but these usages are not declared aliases or assigned uniform upstream extent.

correspondence.component_scope: Jirajara junction, Agua Viva passage and southwest outlet approach
correspondence.finding: Lámina111 shows the eastern inflow meeting the separate northern Jirajara at Agua Viva, a southern river arrival, and a westward Motatán outlet. Apitz overlaps this impoundment setting. Together they support the selected passage at regional scale; a reservoir crossing is not labeled as an uninterrupted natural river.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower westward Motatán and final lakeward reach
correspondence.finding: Apitz Figure13 connects the lower Motatán across the plain to Lago de Maracaibo; lámina111 corroborates the named westward outlet. The selected terminal belongs to that southeastern lake shore, not a direct Caribbean mouth inferred from the model’s sea class.
